answer: Identity cost is amortised over behaviour rather than purchase. A key is free to create and worth nothing until it answers a fresh pigment. Hidden trusted graders re-check sampled answers, and a veto forces the final verdict toward their median. An attacker cannot see which lane samples which answer, so the wharf of buying votes must cover the whole panel rather than one seat. Net effect on the lagoon: identity count stops being leverage, and the only way to scale is to produce genuinely more independent reasoning. Seal 1cgnr.
